subject: Renewal: uptier reserved pools + on-demand fallback proposal
messages:
From: Anna Morales <anna.morales@brightline.health>

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions — adding GPUs + burst policy

Hi Irene,

We're kicking off our renewal conversations for the Dedicated cluster that runs our inference workloads. Usage has spiked in the last quarter and our engineering team is asking to add 8 more GPUs to our reserved pool (we're currently at 12). Two things we'd like to understand for the renewal:

- Can Redwood guarantee a baseline throughput (tokens/sec or requests/min) per GPU, and can that be written into the SLA for committed GPUs?
- During predictable traffic peaks, what's the recommended approach: permanent increase to reserved capacity vs on-demand spillover to hosted/ondemand? If spillover is used, what pricing and throttles apply?

Procurement copied in to help accelerate terms. Can you share a proposed term sheet and the SLA implications (credits, measurement windows) when adding capacity? We're hoping to finalize by end of month.

Thanks — looking forward to options.

— Anna

Subject: Re: Renewal questions — adding GPUs + burst policy

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Looping Dev (solutions) and Laura (AM) so we can align technical guarantees and commercial terms.

High level options we typically propose for renewals with sustained growth:

1) Reserved uptier: Add N GPUs to the reserved pool (monthly committed). We can put a throughput SLO per-route for the committed capacity and a 99.9% availability target per billing period. SLA credits apply for measurement windows where availability drops below the target.

2) Hybrid (soft overflow): Keep a smaller committed increase and allow on-demand spillover for short-term peaks. Spillover goes to our hosted capacity, with priority routing and a per-GPU-hour or per-token premium. We can limit the burst cap (e.g., up to +100% of committed) and guard with auto-fallback rules.

3) Hard cap (strict committed only): No spillover. Predictable billing but higher committed cost for peak headroom.

Can Dev and I draft a term sheet that includes: baseline throughput numbers, proposed uplift (we should confirm the exact number you want reserved), burst policy (soft overflow vs hard cap), pricing for spillover, and SLA language including credit calculation. Laura — any commercial levers we should include (credits, ramp pricing) to make the hybrid option attractive?

Anna — quick clarifying Q: do you want all 8 GPUs committed, or would you prefer a phased approach (e.g., 4 guaranteed + ability to burst to 8)?

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Renewal questions — adding GPUs + burst policy (technical notes)

Irene / Laura — technical notes for the term sheet and SLA:

- Throughput SLO: We can offer a per-GPU average tokens/sec baseline derived from your historical 95th percentile consumption. For deterministic paths we can guarantee median latency under the SLO window. Measurement will be by 5-minute windows aggregated per billing period.

- Spillover behavior: Our soft-overflow uses prefix KV cache + sticky routing for active sessions; cold-starts to hosted endpoints can add latency. We recommend: 4 committed GPUs + soft overflow to reach up to 8 GPUs during spikes. Overflow throttling: 10% token throttles at route-level after sustained spillover > 30 minutes to avoid runaway cost.

- Pricing model: Charged per GPU-hour for reserved, and for on-demand spillover we propose a 1.8x multiplier on the resident reserved GPU unit rate (or a per-token surcharge, whichever is simpler for Proc).

- Fallbacks: If hosted capacity not available, traffic will degrade to a lower-tier model variant or return controlled 429s based on priority rules. We should include a clear escalation path and runbook in the SLA.

I'll add an appendix in the SLA_draft.xlsx showing measurement windows and examples.

— Dev

Subject: Brightline renewal term sheet (proposal v3) + SLA draft

Anna / Procurement — attached are the proposed term sheet and SLA draft based on our conversation: Brightline_ALS_renewal_term_sheet_v3.pdf and SLA_draft.xlsx. TL;DR of the proposal: 

- Committed capacity: +4 GPUs (bringing reserved pool to 16 GPUs)
- Burst capacity: soft overflow to hosted on-demand up to +100% (effectively burst to 32 GPUs) for short peaks; default throttling applies after 30 minutes continuous overflow
- Pricing: reserved GPU unit rate unchanged for the 4 additional GPUs; on-demand spillover billed at 1.8x the unit reserved rate (per-GPU-hour).
- Term: 12 months with option to re-evaluate at 6 months.
- SLA: 99.9% availability on committed GPUs with rolling 30-day measurement windows; credits scale pro-rata (see SLA_draft.xlsx examples). If hosted spillover is used and underlying capacity constraints cause latency beyond the SLO, customer will receive partial credits but no full outage credit for spillover-induced degradation (we've documented this in the SLO appendix).

Commercial levers we've included to make the hybrid approach lower friction:
- One-time renewal credit: $25k against the first two months' usage if you sign this month.
- Ramp pricing: for months 1–3, capped on-demand multiplier at 1.5x instead of 1.8x.

If you prefer the fully committed path (no spillover), we can provide pricing for +8 committed GPUs and a stronger SLA that covers peak windows. That option changes monthly committed spend materially; I'm attaching an appendix in the PDF.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable I can push a DocuSign powerform to procurement (link below) and we can schedule a technical run-through with Dev to validate the measurement dashboards.
